audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Hebrew defense, Damascus encounter retold, Ananias, temple vision, nations commission, crowd reaction, Roman citizenship.

verses.restored: Men, siblings and fathers, hear my defense now to you.

familiar.text: Men, brethren, and fathers, hear ye my defence which I make now unto you.

modern.text: “Brothers and fathers, listen now to my defense before you.”

original.text: Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοὶ καὶ πατέρες, ἀκούσατέ μου τῆς πρὸς ὑμᾶς νυνὶ ἀπολογίας.

verses.restored: Hearing that he addressed them in the Hebrew dialect, they provided even more quiet. He says:

familiar.text: (And when they heard that he spake in the Hebrew tongue to them, they kept the more silence: and he saith,)

modern.text: When they heard him speak to them in Hebrew, they became even more silent. Then Paul declared,

original.text: Ἀκούσαντες δὲ ὅτι τῇ Ἑβραΐδι διαλέκτῳ προσεφώνει αὐτοῖς μᾶλλον παρέσχον ἡσυχίαν. καὶ φησίν·

verses.restored: I am a Judean man, born in Tarsus of Cilicia but brought up in this city, educated at the feet of Gamaliel according to the strictness of the ancestral Law, being zealous for the Divine just as all of you are today.

familiar.text: I am verily a man which am a Jew, born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, yet brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, and taught according to the perfect manner of the law of the fathers, and was zealous toward God, as ye all are this day.

modern.text: “I am a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but raised in this city. I was educated at the feet of Gamaliel in strict conformity to the law of our fathers. I am just as zealous for God as any of you here today.

original.text: ⸀Ἐγώ εἰμι ἀνὴρ Ἰουδαῖος, γεγεννημένος ἐν Ταρσῷ τῆς Κιλικίας, ἀνατεθραμμένος δὲ ἐν τῇ πόλει ταύτῃ παρὰ τοὺς πόδας Γαμαλιήλ, πεπαιδευμένος κατὰ ἀκρίβειαν τοῦ πατρῴου νόμου, ζηλωτὴς ὑπάρχων τοῦ θεοῦ καθὼς πάντες ὑμεῖς ἐστε σήμερον,

verses.restored: I pursued this Way as far as death, binding and handing over to prisons both men and women,

familiar.text: And I persecuted this way unto the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women.

modern.text: I persecuted this Way even to the death, detaining both men and women and throwing them into prison,

original.text: ὃς ταύτην τὴν ὁδὸν ἐδίωξα ἄχρι θανάτου, δεσμεύων καὶ παραδιδοὺς εἰς φυλακὰς ἄνδρας τε καὶ γυναῖκας,

verses.restored: as also the high priest and all the council of elders bear witness to me. From them I received letters to the siblings, and I journeyed to Damascus to bring also those there bound to Jerusalem to be punished.

familiar.text: As also the high priest doth bear me witness, and all the estate of the elders: from whom also I received letters unto the brethren, and went to Damascus, to bring them which were there bound unto Jerusalem, for to be punished.

modern.text: as the high priest and the whole Council can testify about me. I even obtained letters from them to their brothers in Damascus, and I was on my way to apprehend these people and bring them to Jerusalem to be punished.

original.text: ὡς καὶ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς μαρτυρεῖ μοι καὶ πᾶν τὸ πρεσβυτέριον· παρʼ ὧν καὶ ἐπιστολὰς δεξάμενος πρὸς τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς εἰς Δαμασκὸν ἐπορευόμην ἄξων καὶ τοὺς ἐκεῖσε ὄντας δεδεμένους εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἵνα τιμωρηθῶσιν.

verses.restored: It happened to me, as I was journeying and drawing near to Damascus about noon, suddenly from heaven a considerable light flashed around me.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, that, as I made my journey, and was come nigh unto Damascus about noon, suddenly there shone from heaven a great light round about me.

modern.text: About noon as I was approaching Damascus, suddenly a bright light from heaven flashed around me.

original.text: Ἐγένετο δέ μοι πορευομένῳ καὶ ἐγγίζοντι τῇ Δαμασκῷ περὶ μεσημβρίαν ἐξαίφνης ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ περιαστράψαι φῶς ἱκανὸν περὶ ἐμέ,

verses.restored: I fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to me, Saul, Saul, why do you pursue me?

familiar.text: And I fell unto the ground, and heard a voice saying unto me, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?

modern.text: I fell to the ground and heard a voice say to me, ‘Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me?’

original.text: ἔπεσά τε εἰς τὸ ἔδαφος καὶ ἤκουσα φωνῆς λεγούσης μοι· Σαοὺλ Σαούλ, τί με διώκεις;

verses.restored: I answered, Who are you, Lord? He said to me, I am Jesus the Nazarene, whom you pursue.

familiar.text: And I answered, Who art thou, Lord? And he said unto me, I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom thou persecutest.

modern.text: ‘Who are You, Lord?’ I asked. ‘I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you are persecuting,’ He replied.

original.text: ἐγὼ δὲ ἀπεκρίθην· Τίς εἶ, κύριε; εἶπέν τε πρὸς ⸀ἐμέ· Ἐγώ εἰμι Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζωραῖος ὃν σὺ διώκεις.

verses.restored: Those with me beheld the light, but did not understand the voice of the one speaking to me.

familiar.text: And they that were with me saw indeed the light, and were afraid; but they heard not the voice of him that spake to me.

modern.text: My companions saw the light, but they could not understand the voice of the One speaking to me.

original.text: οἱ δὲ σὺν ἐμοὶ ὄντες τὸ μὲν φῶς ⸀ἐθεάσαντο τὴν δὲ φωνὴν οὐκ ἤκουσαν τοῦ λαλοῦντός μοι.

verses.restored: I said, What shall I do, Lord? The Lord said to me, Rise and go into Damascus, and there it will be told to you concerning all things appointed for you to do.

familiar.text: And I said, What shall I do, LORD? And the Lord said unto me, Arise, and go into Damascus; and there it shall be told thee of all things which are appointed for thee to do.

modern.text: Then I asked, ‘What should I do, Lord?’ ‘Get up and go into Damascus,’ He told me. ‘There you will be told all that you have been appointed to do.’

original.text: εἶπον δέ· Τί ποιήσω, κύριε; ὁ δὲ κύριος εἶπεν πρός με· Ἀναστὰς πορεύου εἰς Δαμασκόν, κἀκεῖ σοι λαληθήσεται περὶ πάντων ὧν τέτακταί σοι ποιῆσαι.

verses.restored: Since I was not seeing from the glory of that light, being led by the hand by those with me, I came into Damascus.

familiar.text: And when I could not see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of them that were with me, I came into Damascus.

modern.text: Because the brilliance of the light had blinded me, my companions led me by the hand into Damascus.

original.text: ὡς δὲ οὐκ ἐνέβλεπον ἀπὸ τῆς δόξης τοῦ φωτὸς ἐκείνου, χειραγωγούμενος ὑπὸ τῶν συνόντων μοι ἦλθον εἰς Δαμασκόν.

verses.restored: A certain Ananias, a devout man according to the Law, well witnessed by all the Judeans dwelling there,

familiar.text: And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews which dwelt there,

modern.text: There a man named Ananias, a devout observer of the law who was highly regarded by all the Jews living there,

original.text: Ἁνανίας δέ τις ἀνὴρ ⸀εὐλαβὴς κατὰ τὸν νόμον μαρτυρούμενος ὑπὸ πάντων τῶν κατοικούντων Ἰουδαίων,

verses.restored: came to me, stood by me, and said to me, Brother Saul, see again. And in that very hour I looked up at him.

familiar.text: Came unto me, and stood, and said unto me, Brother Saul, receive thy sight. And the same hour I looked up upon him.

modern.text: came and stood beside me. ‘Brother Saul,’ he said, ‘receive your sight.’ And at that moment I could see him.

original.text: ἐλθὼν πρὸς ⸀ἐμὲ καὶ ἐπιστὰς εἶπέν μοι· Σαοὺλ ἀδελφέ, ἀνάβλεψον· κἀγὼ αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἀνέβλεψα εἰς αὐτόν.

verses.restored: He said, The Divine of our fathers appointed you beforehand to know his will, to see the Righteous One, and to hear a voice from his mouth,

familiar.text: And he said, The God of our fathers hath chosen thee, that thou shouldest know his will, and see that Just One, and shouldest hear the voice of his mouth.

modern.text: Then he said, ‘The God of our fathers has appointed you to know His will, and to see the Righteous One, and to hear His voice.

original.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ὁ θεὸς τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν προεχειρίσατό σε γνῶναι τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἰδεῖν τὸν δίκαιον καὶ ἀκοῦσαι φωνὴν ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ,

verses.restored: because you will be a witness for him to all humans of what you have seen and heard.

familiar.text: For thou shalt be his witness unto all men of what thou hast seen and heard.

modern.text: You will be His witness to everyone of what you have seen and heard.

original.text: ὅτι ἔσῃ μάρτυς αὐτῷ πρὸς πάντας ἀνθρώπους ὧν ἑώρακας καὶ ἤκουσας.

verses.restored: And now why do you delay? Rise, be baptized, and wash away your sins/misalignments, calling upon his name.

familiar.text: And now why tarriest thou? arise, and be baptized, and wash away thy sins, calling on the name of the Lord.

modern.text: And now what are you waiting for? Get up, be baptized, and wash your sins away, calling on His name.’

original.text: καὶ νῦν τί μέλλεις; ἀναστὰς βάπτισαι καὶ ἀπόλουσαι τὰς ἁμαρτίας σου ἐπικαλεσάμενος τὸ ὄνομα ⸀αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: It happened when I returned to Jerusalem and was praying in the temple, that I came to be in a trance

familiar.text: And it came to pass, that, when I was come again to Jerusalem, even while I prayed in the temple, I was in a trance;

modern.text: Later, when I had returned to Jerusalem and was praying at the temple, I fell into a trance

original.text: Ἐγένετο δέ μοι ὑποστρέψαντι εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ προσευχομένου μου ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ γενέσθαι με ἐν ἐκστάσει

verses.restored: and saw him saying to me, Hurry and go out quickly from Jerusalem, because they will not receive your witness concerning me.

familiar.text: And saw him saying unto me, Make haste, and get thee quickly out of Jerusalem: for they will not receive thy testimony concerning me.

modern.text: and saw the Lord saying to me, ‘Hurry! Leave Jerusalem quickly, because the people here will not accept your testimony about Me.’

original.text: καὶ ἰδεῖν αὐτὸν λέγοντά μοι· Σπεῦσον καὶ ἔξελθε ἐν τάχει ἐξ Ἰερουσαλήμ, διότι οὐ παραδέξονταί ⸀σου μαρτυρίαν περὶ ἐμοῦ.

verses.restored: I said, Lord, they themselves know that I was imprisoning and beating in every synagogue those trusting in you.

familiar.text: And I said, Lord, they know that I imprisoned and beat in every synagogue them that believed on thee:

modern.text: ‘Lord,’ I answered, ‘they know very well that in one synagogue after another I imprisoned and beat those who believed in You.

original.text: κἀγὼ εἶπον· Κύριε, αὐτοὶ ἐπίστανται ὅτι ἐγὼ ἤμην φυλακίζων καὶ δέρων κατὰ τὰς συναγωγὰς τοὺς πιστεύοντας ἐπὶ σέ·

verses.restored: And when the blood of Stephen your witness was being poured out, I also stood by and approved, guarding the garments of those killing him.

familiar.text: And when the blood of thy martyr Stephen was shed, I also was standing by, and consenting unto his death, and kept the raiment of them that slew him.

modern.text: And when the blood of Your witness Stephen was shed, I stood there giving my approval and watching over the garments of those who killed him.’

original.text: καὶ ὅτε ⸀ἐξεχύννετο τὸ αἷμα Στεφάνου τοῦ μάρτυρός σου, καὶ αὐτὸς ἤμην ἐφεστὼς καὶ συνευδοκῶν ⸀καὶ φυλάσσων τὰ ἱμάτια τῶν ἀναιρούντων αὐτόν.

verses.restored: He said to me, Go, because I will send you far away to the nations.

familiar.text: And he said unto me, Depart: for I will send thee far hence unto the Gentiles.

modern.text: Then He said to me, ‘Go! I will send you far away to the Gentiles.’” Paul the Roman Citizen

original.text: καὶ εἶπεν πρός με· Πορεύου, ὅτι ἐγὼ εἰς ἔθνη μακρὰν ἐξαποστελῶ σε.

verses.restored: They were listening to him until this word, and they lifted up their voice, saying, Take such a one away from the earth, for it is not fitting for him to live.

familiar.text: And they gave him audience unto this word, and then lifted up their voices, and said, Away with such a fellow from the earth: for it is not fit that he should live.

modern.text: The crowd listened to Paul until he made this statement. Then they lifted up their voices and shouted, “Rid the earth of him! He is not fit to live!”

original.text: Ἤκουον δὲ αὐτοῦ ἄχρι τούτου τοῦ λόγου καὶ ἐπῆραν τὴν φωνὴν αὐτῶν λέγοντες· Αἶρε ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς τὸν τοιοῦτον, οὐ γὰρ καθῆκεν αὐτὸν ζῆν.

verses.restored: As they were crying out, throwing off garments, and tossing dust into the air,

familiar.text: And as they cried out, and cast off their clothes, and threw dust into the air,

modern.text: As they were shouting and throwing off their cloaks and tossing dust into the air,

original.text: ⸀κραυγαζόντων ⸀τε αὐτῶν καὶ ῥιπτούντων τὰ ἱμάτια καὶ κονιορτὸν βαλλόντων εἰς τὸν ἀέρα,

verses.restored: the commander commanded him to be brought into the barracks, saying that he should be examined by flogging, so that he might know for what cause they were shouting against him this way.

familiar.text: The chief captain commanded him to be brought into the castle, and bade that he should be examined by scourging; that he might know wherefore they cried so against him.

modern.text: the commander ordered that Paul be brought into the barracks. He directed that Paul be flogged and interrogated to determine the reason for this outcry against him.

original.text: ἐκέλευσεν ⸂ὁ χιλίαρχος εἰσάγεσθαι αὐτὸν⸃ εἰς τὴν παρεμβολήν, ⸀εἴπας μάστιξιν ἀνετάζεσθαι αὐτὸν ἵνα ἐπιγνῷ διʼ ἣν αἰτίαν οὕτως ἐπεφώνουν αὐτῷ.

verses.restored: But when they stretched him forward with straps, Paul said to the centurion standing by, Is it lawful for you to flog a Roman citizen and uncondemned?

familiar.text: And as they bound him with thongs, Paul said unto the centurion that stood by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman, and uncondemned?

modern.text: But as they stretched him out to strap him down, Paul said to the centurion standing there, “Is it lawful for you to flog a Roman citizen without a trial?”

original.text: ὡς δὲ ⸀προέτειναν αὐτὸν τοῖς ἱμᾶσιν εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν ἑστῶτα ἑκατόνταρχον ὁ Παῦλος· Εἰ ἄνθρωπον Ῥωμαῖον καὶ ἀκατάκριτον ἔξεστιν ὑμῖν μαστίζειν;

verses.restored: Hearing this, the centurion went to the commander and reported, saying, What are you about to do? For this human is Roman.

familiar.text: When the centurion heard that, he went and told the chief captain, saying, Take heed what thou doest: for this man is a Roman.

modern.text: On hearing this, the centurion went and reported it to the commander. “What are you going to do?” he said. “This man is a Roman citizen.”

original.text: ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης προσελθὼν ⸂τῷ χιλιάρχῳ ἀπήγγειλεν⸃ λέγων· ⸀Τί μέλλεις ποιεῖν; ὁ γὰρ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος Ῥωμαῖός ἐστιν.

verses.restored: The commander came and said to him, Tell me, are you Roman? He said, Yes.

familiar.text: Then the chief captain came, and said unto him, Tell me, art thou a Roman? He said, Yea.

modern.text: The commander went to Paul and asked, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?” “Yes,” he answered.

original.text: προσελθὼν δὲ ὁ χιλίαρχος εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Λέγε μοι, ⸀σὺ Ῥωμαῖος εἶ; ὁ δὲ ἔφη· Ναί.

verses.restored: The commander answered, I acquired this citizenship for a large sum. Paul said, But I have been born so.

familiar.text: And the chief captain answered, With a great sum obtained I this freedom. And Paul said, But I was free born.

modern.text: “I paid a high price for my citizenship,” said the commander. “But I was born a citizen,” Paul replied.

original.text: ἀπεκρίθη ⸀δὲ ὁ χιλίαρχος· Ἐγὼ πολλοῦ κεφαλαίου τὴν πολιτείαν ταύτην ἐκτησάμην. ὁ δὲ Παῦλος ἔφη· Ἐγὼ δὲ καὶ γεγέννημαι.

verses.restored: Immediately therefore those about to examine him withdrew from him, and the commander also was afraid, realizing that he was Roman and that he had bound him.

familiar.text: Then straightway they departed from him which should have examined him: and the chief captain also was afraid, after he knew that he was a Roman, and because he had bound him.

modern.text: Then those who were about to interrogate Paul stepped back, and the commander himself was alarmed when he realized that he had put a Roman citizen in chains.

original.text: εὐθέως οὖν ἀπέστησαν ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ οἱ μέλλοντες αὐτὸν ἀνετάζειν· καὶ ὁ χιλίαρχος δὲ ἐφοβήθη ἐπιγνοὺς ὅτι Ῥωμαῖός ἐστιν καὶ ὅτι ⸂αὐτὸν ἦν⸃ δεδεκώς.

verses.restored: On the next day, wishing to know the certainty of why he was accused by the Judeans, he released him and commanded the chief priests and all the council to gather, and bringing Paul down, he stood him among them.

familiar.text: On the morrow, because he would have known the certainty wherefore he was accused of the Jews, he loosed him from his bands, and commanded the chief priests and all their council to appear, and brought Paul down, and set him before them.

modern.text: The next day the commander, wanting to learn the real reason Paul was accused by the Jews, released him and ordered the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin to assemble. Then he brought Paul down and had him stand before them.

original.text: Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον βουλόμενος γνῶναι τὸ ἀσφαλὲς τὸ τί κατηγορεῖται ⸀ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἔλυσεν ⸀αὐτόν, καὶ ἐκέλευσεν ⸀συνελθεῖν τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ ⸀πᾶν τὸ ⸀συνέδριον, καὶ καταγαγὼν τὸν Παῦλον ἔστησεν εἰς αὐτούς.
